pharm: Bifunctional nitrogen-mustard alkylator with a benzimidazole ring; forms interstrand DNA crosslinks causing cell death in both quiescent and dividing cells
quick: Indolent NHL 120 mg/m2 IV over 60 min on Days 1-2 of a 21-day cycle (up to 8 cycles)
Can cause fetal harm - avoid; use contraception
Do not breastfeed during and after treatment
Do not use if CrCl <30 mL/min
Do not use if bilirubin >3x ULN (or 1.5-3x ULN with AST/ALT 2.5-10x ULN)
CBC, renal/hepatic function, infusion reactions, infection, TLS, skin
summary: Bendamustine hydrochloride is an intravenous bifunctional alkylating agent (a mechlorethamine derivative with a purine-like benzimidazole ring) indicated for indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma that has progressed during or within six months of a rituximab-containing regimen, and (per related labeling) for chronic lymphocytic leukemia. The typical NHL dose is 120 mg/m2 IV over 60 minutes on Days 1 and 2 of a 21-day cycle for up to 8 cycles, with dose modifications for hematologic and non-hematologic toxicity. Major risks are myelosuppression, infections (including reactivation), progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, severe anaphylactic/infusion reactions, tumor lysis syndrome, severe skin reactions (SJS/DRESS/TEN), hepatotoxicity, extravasation injury and embryo-fetal toxicity.
indications: Indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) that has progressed during or within six months of treatment with rituximab or a rituximab-containing regimen
Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) (per related bendamustine labeling)

dosage.d: 120 mg/m2 infused over 60 minutes on Days 1 and 2 of a 21-day cycle
dosage.t: Days 1-2 every 21 days, up to 8 cycles

dosage.d: 100 mg/m2 over 30 minutes on Days 1 and 2 of a 28-day cycle
dosage.t: Days 1-2 every 28 days, up to 6 cycles

dosage.d: For Grade 4 toxicity reduce to 90 mg/m2 on Days 1-2; if it recurs reduce to 60 mg/m2
dosage.n: Resume when ANC >=1 x10^9/L and platelets >=75 x10^9/L

dosage.d: For Grade 3 or greater toxicity reduce to 90 mg/m2; if it recurs reduce to 60 mg/m2
dosage.n: Delay for Grade 4 hematologic or clinically significant >=Grade 2 non-hematologic toxicity

admin: Administer as an IV infusion over 60 minutes (NHL) using the reconstituted/diluted solution per labeling; monitor the infusion site to avoid extravasation

Premedicate (antihistamine, antipyretic, corticosteroid) in subsequent cycles for patients with prior Grade 1-2 infusion reactions; consider TLS prophylaxis (hydration, allopurinol) in high-risk patients
Hazardous drug - use gloves and eye protection; wash skin/mucosa thoroughly if contact occurs
Delay or reduce dose for Grade 4 hematologic or significant non-hematologic toxicity and restart based on count recovery
moa: Bendamustine is a bifunctional mechlorethamine (nitrogen-mustard) derivative containing a purine-like benzimidazole ring. Its electrophilic alkyl groups form covalent bonds with nucleophilic DNA moieties, producing interstrand DNA crosslinks that lead to cell death via multiple pathways; it is active against both quiescent and dividing cells. The exact mechanism remains unknown.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity (anaphylactic/anaphylactoid reactions) to bendamustine or to excipients (polyethylene glycol 400, absolute ethanol, sodium hydroxide, monothioglycerol)
relative: Hepatic impairment with bilirubin >3x ULN, or bilirubin 1.5-3x ULN with AST/ALT 2.5-10x ULN (do not use)
Active serious infection or severe myelosuppression

preg: Based on its mechanism and animal data (embryo-fetal mortality, structural abnormalities, growth alterations), bendamustine can cause fetal harm. Advise females of reproductive potential of the risk and to use effective contraception; advise males with female partners of reproductive potential to use contraception.
lact: There are no data on the presence of bendamustine in human milk; because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed child, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment.
renal: Use with caution; do not use in patients with creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min (not studied).
hepatic: Use with caution in mild hepatic impairment. Do not use in patients with total bilirubin >3x ULN, or bilirubin 1.5-3x ULN with AST or ALT 2.5-10x ULN. Monitor liver chemistry tests before and during treatment.

moderate: CYP1A2 inhibitors - may increase bendamustine concentrations and toxicity; consider alternatives
CYP1A2 inducers - may decrease bendamustine concentrations and efficacy; consider alternatives
minor: Other myelosuppressive agents / radiation - additive marrow suppression
interactions.alcohol: Avoid - the formulation contains ethanol and alcohol adds GI/hepatic stress
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate liver chemistries and uric acid; monitor

serious: Tumor lysis syndrome with acute renal failure
Severe skin reactions (SJS, DRESS, TEN - some fatal)
emergency: Rash, facial swelling or difficulty breathing during/after infusion (anaphylaxis/infusion reaction)
Fever or signs of infection with low counts
New confusion, memory loss, trouble speaking/walking or vision loss (PML)
Reduced urine output, flank pain, metabolic derangement (tumor lysis)

monitoring: CBC with differential (delay/reduce dose per ANC and platelet recovery)
Renal function and electrolytes/uric acid (tumor lysis syndrome) in high-risk patients
Liver chemistry tests before and during treatment
Infusion reactions during and after administration; infection signs and fever
Skin for severe cutaneous reactions; infusion-site for extravasation
counsel: This treatment lowers your blood counts - have regular blood tests and report fever, signs of infection, unusual bleeding or bruising or marked fatigue
Report rash, facial swelling or trouble breathing during or soon after the infusion immediately
Report any confusion, memory or speech problems, weakness or vision changes (could indicate a serious brain infection)
Report severe or worsening rash, itching, blisters or mouth/eye sores
Use effective contraception during treatment; do not breastfeed
Tell your team about all your medicines
pk: Cytotoxic effect over the treatment cycle; Cmax at end of infusion
Parent compound ~40 minutes; active metabolites M3 ~3 h and M4 ~30 min
Per cyclical 21- or 28-day schedule; high protein binding (94-96%)
Refrigerate 2-8 C; retain in original carton to protect from light; hazardous drug
pearls: Severe and sometimes fatal myelosuppression - delay/reduce dose based on ANC and platelet recovery; monitor counts each cycle
Severe anaphylactic/infusion reactions can occur - premedicate in later cycles after milder reactions and discontinue for severe reactions
Watch for tumor lysis syndrome (especially first cycle) and progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (new neurologic/cognitive symptoms)
Avoid in CrCl <30 mL/min and in significant hepatic impairment (bilirubin >3x ULN); formulation contains ethanol
missed: Bendamustine is given by clinicians on a fixed cycle schedule; there is no patient self-administered make-up dose. Missed or delayed infusions are rescheduled by the oncology team based on toxicity and count recovery.
overdose: No specific antidote exists. Reported single doses up to 280 mg/m2 caused dose-limiting ECG changes (QT prolongation, sinus tachycardia, ST/T-wave changes, conduction block). Management is supportive with monitoring of hematologic parameters and ECGs.
